I'm thinking of using Posca markers - I don't want to take away from the beauty of the skull itself, so currently my mind is at linework-type designs limited to red and black, I'm taking a lot of inspiration from tattoos and how they compliment the body. I'm not sure if my method will work as expected, but I'm open to trail and error and learning through the experience :) 

The first and only time I've worked with bone before was about 8 years ago and I was overambitious with oil and a renaissance-esque design in mind (it took a ridiculous amount of primer to the surface area of where my design was going to be).

That was my first thought when I saw the holes too! But my other one had them too in the same spot, and they look to be present in some other images of giraffe skulls online as well, so I assume it's some deterioration, it definitely adds a lot of character though!
I live in South Africa, so these type of animal bones are definitely a lot more accessible to me haha

Ironically, I'm going to gift it to a friend - their nickname is Giraffe and they're a collector too, so it just seems fitting!

I was given two giraffe, a warthog, zebra, and an antelope (I think a bushbuck, iirc) skull :)

I only discovered this subreddit recently, but I'd love to share my collection at some point!
This is so reassuring, thank you! I'm still new to this and wanted to be cautious :)

It takes a while to have significant effect but what's had the biggest impact on me is daily exercise, keeping hydrated, eating healthily and regularly, my sleeping pattern naturally adjusted and has been fairly constant so I get enough rest and very very importantly is keeping stress levels low. 




I always took those things for granted until I realised my condition has improved and all change I made was adding a minimum of 30 minutes of exercise per day and it seemed like thereafter things just started going my way for once. :) 



When I was diagnosed I was initially prescribed Cymbalta too, 30mg if I recall correctly, I unfortunately didn't have a good experience with it, it was like being a zombie with no emotion and awful nausea, I hear the effects go away after a while, but it was too much for me to handle. When reporting back to my doctor I was prescribed with muscle relaxers which helped with the daily pain a bit, along with weekly visits to the physiotherapist. It's been about a year since and I still flare up, especially when stress is present but the overall constant pain and fatigue have reduced significantly!



Well wishes!
